title: POC scoping - Quality eval plan
summary: POC scoping focused on quality evaluation plan for Lifeline Medical. Discussed golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks, scoring methodology, workload sizing and benchmarks, timeline for deliverables and security requirements. Agreed next steps and owners for benchmark runs and prompt handoff.
next_steps: Samir to run initial latency/cost benchmark (1k requests) and share results
Julia to provide golden prompt set + expected outputs by 2026-08-05
Maya to send POC SOW and pricing options
Priya to review security docs and confirm any additional controls
action_items: Samir: run 1k request latency/cost benchmark and share raw logs by 2026-08-03
Julia: provide 50-100 golden prompts and expected output snippets by 2026-08-05
Maya: send security compliance pack (SOC2, ISO) and POC SOW by 2026-07-31
Priya: confirm KMS/HSM requirements and data residency constraints by 2026-08-06
transcript: 00:00 Maya: okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. this is Maya from Redwood, i have Samir and Luca with me. 00:08 Tom: hey thanks, Tom here — running a bit behind, appreciate you guys fitting us in. 00:13 Maya: no worries, we'll do a quick agenda: align on success criteria, walk through workload sizing for the poc, define the quality eval plan — golden prompts, regression and hallucination checks, scoring — and then timelines. 00:26 Julia: sounds good. our priority is safety and accuracy for clinical summarization flows, second is latency for interactive use by nurses. 00:34 Samir: great. can you give a quick overview of current stack and throughput? like typical concurrency and token sizes? 00:41 Julia: sure. we process batch of discharge summaries and also live chat triage. typical live prompt is about 120-250 tokens, discharge summaries go up to 3k tokens. concurrency for chat peaks around 40 concurrent sessions during day shifts, batch runs overnight, roughly 2-3k docs/day. 01:03 Samir: okay so mixed workload; for scoring and quality eval we should separate interactive latency SLOs vs batch throughput. i'm thinking we run two benchmark profiles: 1) interactive 128-token median with 50 concurrent sessions and 2) batch long-form up to 3k tokens with sustained throughput. 01:19 Tom: that works. cost is a concern — we want to compare hosted vs dedicated, and if quantized models would reduce cost w/o hurting clinical fidelity. 01:29 Maya: yep, part of Redwood Optimize is recommendations on quantization and batching. for the POC we'll include a cost/latency table. 01:35 Priya: on security side, we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration and audit logs. also data residency — all PHI must stay in us-east region. 01:45 Maya: we support customer-managed KMS and private deployments; we'll surface the security pack. i'll follow up. 01:51 Julia: on quality eval: our definition of success is <2% clinically significant hallucinations on the golden set, >92% format fidelity for structured outputs, and median latency <400ms for interactive. 02:06 Samir: nice crisp criteria. for hallucination checks we typically include both automated entity hallucination detection and manual review on a sample. recommend the golden prompts include edge cases: ambiguous references, missing context, and truncated notes. 02:18 Julia: yes, we'll include tricky examples — e.g., typos in medication names, incomplete sentences. 02:24 Luca: quick note — transcription may show "K-V cash" in some quick notes, the runtime has KV cache op-tims not K-V cash, but anyway. 02:33 Tom: (laughs) yeah sometimes auto transcripts butcher the tech terms. 02:37 Samir: for scoring approach we propose a blended metric: 50% clinical correctness (human-annotated), 30% format fidelity (automated schema checks), 20% hallucination penalty. we can run a confusion-matrix style evaluation for entity-level recall/precision. 02:52 Julia: for clinical correctness what's the annotation process? we have a small internal reviewer team — 3 clinicians — will they do gold annotations? 02:59 Maya: ideal: you provide the expected outputs for golden prompts (so we can do automated string/semantic match) and then we run human annotation for a stratified sample for clinical correctness. we can also run ROUGE/BERTscore as a soft signal but won't rely on it exclusively. 03:15 Priya: on format checks, we require strict JSON schema output for discharge summaries fields (dx_code, med_list, follow_up) — failures are unacceptable. we need automated schema validation and a failure rate threshold. 03:27 Samir: we will implement schema validators in the eval harness. we'll record failures and categorize them as minor (formatting) vs major (missing required field or malformed JSON). 03:36 Julia: for regression tests — we want to capture pre-POC baseline with your current model (if hosted) or our baseline model outputs, then run weekly regression runs to ensure no drift. 03:46 Maya: agreed. we'll store baseline outputs and run automated diffs. any regression that increases hallucination metric by >1% triggers a manual review and rollback to fallback model. 03:57 Tom: question — what's the plan for golden prompts volume? 04:01 Julia: i think 100 golden prompts is our initial target: 50 interactive, 50 long-form. 04:08 Samir: that sounds reasonable. also we'll augment those with 500 synthetic prompts for stress testing. 04:14 Maya: timeline-wise, if you provide the golden prompts and security checklist by Aug 5, we can spin up the POC infra, run initial benchmarks by Aug 10-12 and deliver a mid-POC report by Aug 18. final report and recommended rollout by Aug 28. does that fit? 04:30 Julia: timeline ok but need to confirm clinician availability for annotations by mid-Aug. i'll confirm. 04:35 Priya: also need to review data handling in private deployment. if we go with dedicated pool or private VPC we need a quick architecture doc. 04:44 Maya: i'll attach our private deployment architecture and detail on KMS/HSM flows. 04:49 Tom: for benchmarks, what exact metrics will you output? 04:52 Samir: we'll provide median latency, p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and throughput under sustained load, plus accuracy metrics from the eval harness. 05:02 Julia: about hallucinations — can you detect hallucination automatically? sometimes it's subtle. 05:06 Samir: we can detect many hallucinations via entity mismatch and hallucination classifiers, but we will couple this with manual review for clinical judgement. automated detection will flag probable hallucs for sampling. 05:17 Luca: note: some model names in our catalog are shown as "Redwood-Chat-XL" in the UI but internally it's a different ver. we'll clarify model vering in the SOW. 05:26 Tom: how do we handle fallback/rollout if a new model fails the eval? 05:30 Maya: we'll configure rollout policies: canary -> monitor quality metrics -> automatic rollback if hallucination or format failures exceed thresholds. we'll include that in the POC so you can see behavior. 05:41 Julia: can we get an eval sheet template? 05:43 Maya: yes, i'll send the evaluation spreadsheet with scoring columns (clinical correctness, format fidelity, hallucination flag, comments). 05:50 Priya: security question: do you retain logs? we need audit logs but not long-term PHI retention. 05:55 Maya: we support token-level redaction and retention controls; audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM; retention policies are configurable. 06:02 Tom: any blockers on our side? 06:04 Julia: clinician time and compiling golden prompts are the main ones. 06:07 Maya: recap — action items: Samir runs benchmarks (1k interactive + batch tests) and shares results; Julia provides golden prompts by Aug 5; Maya sends SOW, security docs, and eval spreadsheet by July 31; Priya confirms KMS/residency by Aug 6. 06:20 Tom: okay looks good. let's schedule checkpoint after initial benchmarks. 06:24 Maya: will set up meeting for Aug 13 to review initial results. thanks everyone. 06:29 (call ends)
